Jacobin.author: Jeff Fuller

Jacobin.title: Medieval Egypt Was No Stranger to Class War
Jacobin.summary: Egypt in the Middle Ages was steeply class stratified. When the rains failed, the rich dined on hoarded grain while the starving poor ate grass. Periodically, the masses would erupt in revolt — sometimes with petitions, other times with stones.
Jacobin.author: Nicholas Liu

Jacobin.title: Mike Wallace, Gotham’s Chronicler

Jacobin.author: Joel Feingold

Jacobin.title: Profits Are Soaring. Workers’ Share of Income Is Sinking.
Jacobin.summary: Working people’s share of national income has fallen to a record low, even as corporate profits soar to unthinkable new heights. The trend reflects decades of eroded worker power, and reversing it will take a revitalized labor movement.
Jacobin.author: Conor Lynch

Jacobin.title: Isabella Weber on How to Defeat the Far Right
Jacobin.summary: Key to a long-term solution to defeating the far right is an economic program that guarantees security to all, including the affordability of housing and other essential components of a dignified life, Isabella Weber tells Jacobin.
Jacobin.author: Isabella Weber, Bartolomeo Sala

Jacobin.title: The Green Party Will Regain Momentum if It Keeps Its Nerve

Jacobin.author: Daniel Finn

Jacobin.title: How a Canadian Union Finally Bested Walmart

Jacobin.author: Benjamin Y. Fong

Jacobin.author: Molly Judd

Jacobin.title: The Political Economy of Cognitive Dissonance

Jacobin.author: Peter Dorman
